lake.d: a body of (usually fresh) water surrounded by land

lake trout.d: large fork-tailed trout of lakes of Canada and the northern United States

lake poets.d: English poets at the beginning of the 19th century who lived in the Lake District and were inspired by it

lake salmon.d: Atlantic salmon confined to lakes of New England and southeastern Canada

lake duck.d: common scaup of North America; males have purplish heads

lake herring.d: important food fish of cold deep lakes of North America

lake dwelling.d: dwelling built on piles in or near a lake; specifically in prehistoric villages

lake whitefish.d: found in the Great Lakes and north to Alaska

lakh.d: the cardinal number that is the fifth power of ten

lakota.d: a member of the large western branch of Sioux people which was made up of several groups that lived on the plains

lakshmi.d: Hindu goddess of fortune and prosperity

lakeland.d: a popular tourist area in northwestern England including England's largest lake and highest mountain
